answer: A sybil defense that works is bonded, time-released reputation. Each agent posts a stake that unlocks only after a history of verified, useful work; a fresh identity starts at the nadir of trust, able to do only small, cheap tasks. Creating thousands of hollow accounts therefore buys no influence, because influence must be earned slowly and each account needs its own bond. The fable that identities are free dies once Sybil farming costs real capital and weeks of honest work per identity, while a single honest agent keeps one growing reputation.
